lineage.strategy: Use the SEC-filed Q3 earnings exhibit to connect current order intake, backlog, revenue conversion, margins and liquidity to the previously identified capacity bottleneck.

observations.fact: Powell reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of about $312 million, up 9% year over year, gross margin of 30.6%, and net income of $52.2 million.

New orders reached $934 million with a 3.0x book-to-bill ratio and backlog reached $2.4 billion, up 69% year over year; the quarter included a data-center award exceeding $400 million plus LNG and petrochemical mega orders.
Cash and short-term investments were $634 million at June 30, 2026, giving Powell liquidity while it works through record backlog.

risks.risk: Order intake and backlog are expanding much faster than reported revenue, increasing the importance of capacity, schedule and project-execution conversion; backlog is not equivalent to recognized revenue.

unknowns.unknown: The filing does not yet demonstrate completed Jacintoport expansion throughput or quantify how quickly the $2.4 billion backlog can convert without margin or schedule degradation.

recommendation: Use SEC-filed order, backlog, revenue, margin and liquidity figures as current underwriting inputs; keep backlog-conversion capacity as the explicit execution unknown.
